additional_info.subject: RE: 0375775 - ID0375775-DC/Si-D/BE-[MP / PD 170001230] Charger is derating CRM:00641000636
additional_info.body:
Dear Mr. Marnic,
Hope you are doing well
After conducting a thorough investigation, we have determined that the charger is functioning as expected and in compliance with ISO 15118 and DIN 70121 standards.
From the logs provided by you, it is evident that the key factor is the alignment between the EV_TarCur[A] and the EVSE_NowCur[A].
To elaborate, the EV (vehicle) is requesting a current of 200 A (either on DC1 or DC2). This request is influenced by various factors such as temperature, State of Charge (SoC), and battery health. The EVSE (charger) is attempting to provide the requested current to the best of its capability.
If there had been any issues with the charging process, an error would have been recorded. However, since no such error has appeared, it suggests that the system is operating correctly.
Kindly refer the published Knowledge article as well ,
https://isp.crm4.dynamics.com/main.aspx?appid=582042be-d464-ed11-9562a000d3ab780dd&forceUCI=1&newWindow=true&pagetype=entityrecord&etn=knowledgearticle&id=a9d09d20-a464-4c8a-b407-558c04abbd17
Please let me know if further analysis is required.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Abhinav Malokar

additional_info.subject: 0375775 - ID0375775-DC/Si-D/BE-[MP / PD 170001230] Charger is derating CRM:00641000636
additional_info.body:
Hi Lorenz,
Looking back at the email I previously sent I notice that was incorrect, regarding these photos below, the charger is indeed ready to provide 300kW as we see in the parameter EVSE_DesPwr=300kW.
So this means that the EV itself was limiting the power by the current, it only requested 326 A which results in a lower power output.
There's also something that you need to keep in mind:
Imagine that 2 cars come to charge:
EV1 has 50% SoC and EV2 has 10%:
Since EV1 SoC is lower than 60%, it will request maximum power to the charger, let's imagine 220kW
EV2 will only have 80kW available for him, until the first reaches 60% SoC
After EV1 reaches 60% SoC it will release one more group resulting in
DC1: 140kW
DC2: 160kW
I assume that this might be the problem as for the customer it's like a derating.
If we cannot test these specific scenarios, from the logs I show below, there is absolutely nothing wrong.
What do you want to do next?
I will wait for your feedback.
Best regards,
Francisco
